claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Alex Moore is a high-confidence match to the Chicago-born Army officer who transferred to OSS in January 1945.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Official CIA history documents Alex Moore as a first lieutenant, Army interrogation officer, January 1945 OSS transferee, and X-2 administrative officer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact name, lieutenant rank, direct OSS service, January 1945 transfer chronology, and a specific personnel-file reference form a strong identity chain.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources trace Moore from pre-OSS Army service into OSS and identify an earlier Red Cross affiliation.
claims.match_notes: The direct official history is substantially more specific than the rejected name-only newspaper candidates. Box 534 remains the direct personnel-file pointer.

claims.claim_text: Alex Moore's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was a U.S. Army military-intelligence interrogation team in France and Germany.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Moore remained with this team until he transferred to OSS in January 1945.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA History Staff explicitly dates Moore's transfer from the interrogation team to OSS in January 1945.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The official account matches the indexed name and lieutenant rank and directly identifies Moore's OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate predecessor: the source says he remained with the Army team until the OSS transfer.
claims.match_notes: Published as a military assignment, never as a civilian employer. Exact team designation is not supplied in the source.

sources.locator_override: Pages 45-46, OSS and Sixth Army Group SCI context

claims.claim_text: Before Army service, Alex Moore served with the American Red Cross in France and England during the early war years.
claims.evidence_excerpt: served with the American Red Cross for the first years of the war
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official biography places Moore with the Red Cross before his fall 1942 Army enlistment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: This statement appears in the same detailed official biography that identifies his OSS transfer and assignments.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar affiliation ending before Army enlistment; it is not shown to be the immediate pre-OSS role.
claims.match_notes: The source does not establish whether the Red Cross relationship was paid employment or volunteer service, so the relationship remains unknown.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Dan T. Moore is a high-confidence match to Dan Tyler Moore Jr., the Cleveland federal administrator brought into OSS by William Donovan.
claims.evidence_excerpt: William Donovan brought Moore to Washington as a civilian major in the new OSS
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Case Western's institutional biography joins the full name, Cleveland SEC and civilian-defense chronology, and direct OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The distinctive indexed name, full-name expansion, Cleveland federal posts, and explicit Donovan-to-OSS account provide multiple corroborating identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources document his federal assignments through 1942 and then his wartime OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The rejected Captain Dan T. Moore newspaper item lacked an explicit OSS bridge. The institutional chronology is the controlling identity source.

sources.locator_override: PDF page 327, row 12, Box 534, archival location 230/86/37/01

claims.claim_text: Dan Tyler Moore Jr.'s best-supported last civilian government affiliation before OSS was the SEC's Cleveland regional office, which he administered from 1939 to 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The SEC Historical Society roster dates Moore's Cleveland regional-administrator tenure; official and institutional sources corroborate the office and subsequent OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The full name, Cleveland office, dates, and direct OSS biography identify the same person with high confidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded through 1942, immediately before OSS-era service; a concurrent civilian-defense assignment prevents a claim about exact final-day ordering.
claims.match_notes: This is classified as a government assignment. It is the best-supported last civilian government post, not a private-sector employer, and the overlap is shown rather than collapsed.

claims.claim_text: Dan Tyler Moore Jr. also headed a Cleveland civilian-defense regional office while retaining his SEC role in 1942.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Moore ran both the Cleveland SEC and Civil Defense regional offices
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Case Western and a contemporary Congressional Record discussion document overlapping SEC and civilian-defense responsibilities before his OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The same full-name institutional biography connects both Cleveland posts to OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to 1942, but the evidence does not establish whether this or the SEC assignment ended last.
claims.match_notes: Shown as an overlapping government assignment and visibly qualified; it is not labeled a private employer.
